newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle slip, feeders fall after new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle slip, feeders fall after new highs.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were knocked to lower closes by market sentiment that cash cattle prices have reached a top for the time being, while feeder cattle futures tumbled on profit taking after posting new contract highs early, traders said.

Live cattle futures ended 0.375 to 0.075 cent per lb lower with June off 0.325 at 65.725 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 0.250 to off 0.450 cent with only May up and August off most at 77.500 cents. May feeders posted a new high of 76.550 cents early with January through April setting highs before falling.
Futures moved lower late as more traders were swept up in the idea that the seasonal cash market top was in when cattle sold last week at $69.00 per cwt.

Several sources noted that increased cattle supplies loom. Cash beef prices have already begun to slip following completion of beef buying for Memorial Day advertisements and packers will need less cattle soon.
The market is also starting to look ahead to Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report which is expected to show larger than year ago on feed numbers, they added.
Analysts' estimates for May 1 on-feed cattle ranged from 108 to 111 percent of last year.
Placement estimates ranged from 104.9 to 127.5 percent and marketings 98.6 to 104 percent.
RBH, Rand Financials, R.J. O'Brien and CIS sold June late. Refco, Shatkin and RBH sold August and Cargill bought, traders said. Rosenthal Collins sold August early.
In live cattle options, one trader actively sold June 66 calls which lowered the volatility by one percent to nine percent. Commercials sold August 68 calls, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures jumped to new contract highs early, pulled up by a strong tone to cash feeders, but futures fell late as profit taking developed. Sell stops added to the setback before scattered buying pared losses, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index surged $1.93 higher to $75.29 per cwt, the highest level since February 1, 1995.
Profit taking increased when corn futures rallied to net gains and live cattle futures eased further, they said.

"They (traders) are counting on very good cattle prices and they are counting on very cheap feed costs to justify these types of feeder cattle prices and with fed cattle prices starting to look a little weaker, that might knock one leg of the stool out," said Karl Skold, director of research for Frontier Risk Management.
Dean Witter and FIMAT Futures USA bought August while Refco bought May early.

Selling by R.J. O'Brien and Cargill Investor Services hit sell stops late before local buying pared losses. Cargill Investor Services early spread long December and February live cattle/short August feeders, pit sources said.
